cards.title: The island of the Lenape
lines: Manhattan lies in Lenapehoking, the land of the Munsee, Lenape and Wappinger peoples.

cards.title: Hudson's voyage
lines: Sailing for the Dutch on the Halve Maen, Henry Hudson explores the bay and the river that will carry his name.

cards.title: Families land
lines: In May 1624 the Dutch West India Company lands 30 families in New Netherland, some on Governors Island.

cards.title: The purchase of Manhattan
lines: Peter Minuit, director from 1626, is credited with buying the island from Lenape representatives for goods worth 60 guilders.

cards.title: Enslaved labor
lines: The first enslaved Africans in New Amsterdam help build the fort and clear the land.

cards.title: A city with a wall
lines: New Amsterdam receives municipal rights on February 2, 1653.
A wall along today's Wall Street stands until 1699.

cards.title: New York
lines: English forces seize the town in 1664 and rename it for the Duke of York.
About 2,500 of New Netherland's nearly 9,000 colonists live in the town.

cards.title: New Orange
lines: The Dutch retake the city in August 1673 and rename it.
The Treaty of Westminster returns it to England in 1674.

cards.title: A first count
lines: A 1698 count finds 4,937 people in the city.

cards.title: The Stamp Act Congress
lines: Delegates from most of the British colonies meet in City Hall in October 1765 to answer the Stamp Act.

cards.title: The British land
lines: Redcoats under General Howe land on Manhattan on September 15, 1776; the armies fight at Harlem Heights the next day.
The city stays in British hands until 1783.

cards.title: Evacuation Day
lines: British forces leave New York on November 25, 1783, after the Treaty of Paris.

cards.title: A capital for the young republic
lines: The Confederation Congress meets in City Hall from 1785.
Congress leaves for Philadelphia in 1790.

cards.title: The Buttonwood Agreement
lines: On May 17, 1792, 24 brokers sign the pact that grows into the New York Stock Exchange.

cards.title: A grid for the island
lines: The Commissioners' Plan of 1811 lays a grid of streets over Manhattan between Houston Street and 155th Street.

cards.title: The Collect Pond disappears
lines: Landfill finishes in 1811 and middle-class homes rise on the old pond.

cards.title: The Erie Canal opens
lines: The canal opens on October 26, 1825, linking the Atlantic to the Great Lakes.

cards.title: Croton water
lines: The Croton Aqueduct, built 1837 to 1842, brings water by gravity 41 miles to reservoirs in Manhattan.

cards.title: The tallest spire
lines: Trinity Church, built 1839 to 1846, is the tallest building in New York until 1890.

cards.title: High Bridge
lines: Water begins to flow across High Bridge in May 1848; it is the city's oldest major bridge.

cards.title: Immigrant metropolis
lines: Castle Garden becomes the immigrant depot: more than 7.5 million people arrive there between 1855 and 1890.

cards.title: Seneca Village is razed
lines: Founded in 1825 by free Black landowners, the village is torn down in 1857 to make room for Central Park.

cards.title: Central Park opens
lines: The first areas of Central Park open to the public in late 1858; the park is completed in 1876.

cards.title: The Draft Riots
lines: Draft riots rage from July 13 to 16, 1863; mobs burn the Colored Orphan Asylum on Fifth Avenue.

cards.title: Grand Central Depot
lines: The first Grand Central station opens in 1871; today's terminal replaces it in 1913.

cards.title: St. Patrick's Cathedral
lines: The cathedral is dedicated on May 25, 1879; its spires follow in 1888.

cards.title: Liberty Enlightening the World
lines: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated on October 28, 1886, on what was then Bedloe's Island.

cards.title: Ellis Island
lines: The immigration station opens in 1892; until 1954 about 12 million people are processed there.

cards.title: Five boroughs, one city
lines: On January 1, 1898, New York merges with Brooklyn, western Queens and Staten Island.

cards.title: The Flatiron Building
lines: The Flatiron Building opens on October 1, 1902, at 285 feet.

cards.title: The Williamsburg Bridge
lines: The Williamsburg Bridge opens in December 1903 and holds the longest suspension span in the world until 1924.

cards.title: The subway opens
lines: The first subway line opens on October 27, 1904.

cards.title: The Queensboro Bridge
lines: The bridge to Queens opens on March 30, 1909.

cards.title: The Manhattan Bridge
lines: The Manhattan Bridge opens to traffic on December 31, 1909; subway trains follow in 1915.

cards.title: Pennsylvania Station
lines: The station opens in 1910 and gives travelers from the south direct rail access to Manhattan for the first time.

cards.title: The Triangle fire
lines: On March 25, 1911, fire sweeps the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory in the Asch Building near Washington Square.

cards.title: Grand Central Terminal
lines: Grand Central Terminal opens in 1913 on the site of two earlier stations.

cards.title: The Woolworth Building
lines: The Woolworth Building opens in April 1913 and is the tallest building in the world until 1930.

cards.title: Yankee Stadium
lines: Built in 1922 and 1923, the stadium opens in the Bronx.

cards.title: The race to the sky
lines: 40 Wall Street, the Chrysler Building and the Empire State Building compete to be the tallest in the world.

cards.title: The Chrysler Building
lines: The Chrysler Building opens in May 1930, 1,046 feet tall, in a race with 40 Wall Street and the Empire State Building.

cards.title: The George Washington Bridge
lines: The bridge opens on October 25, 1931, with the longest main span in the world.

cards.title: Rockefeller Center
lines: Construction starts in 1931 and the first buildings open in 1933; the core is complete by 1939.

cards.title: The Cloisters
lines: The Cloisters museum opens in Fort Tryon Park on May 10, 1938.

cards.title: Home of the United Nations
lines: The United Nations headquarters is completed in 1952 on the East River.

cards.title: Penn Station is demolished
lines: Demolition of the station above ground begins in 1963 and ends by 1966; the loss galvanizes the preservation movement.

cards.title: The 1977 blackout
lines: On July 13 and 14, 1977, a blackout hits most of the city, followed by looting and arson.

cards.title: September 11, 2001
lines: The Twin Towers of the World Trade Center are destroyed in a terrorist attack.

cards.title: Rebuilding
lines: Work on One World Trade Center begins on April 27, 2006.

cards.title: Hudson Yards
lines: Construction begins in 2012 on platforms over the working rail yard on the far West Side.

cards.title: Hurricane Sandy
lines: On October 29, 2012, the storm surge floods streets, tunnels and subway lines.

cards.title: A new skyline
lines: 432 Park Avenue, finished in 2015, is the tallest residential building in the world when completed; Central Park Tower follows in 2020.
